title: Introduction to rosario
text: rosario package implements null model analysis quantify concurrent temporal niche overlap (.e., activity phenology) among biological identities (e.g., individuals, populations, species) using Rosario randomization algorithm (Castro-Arellano et al. 2010). vignette introduces main functions typical workflow.

title: Introduction to rosario
text: package includes example dataset, ex1, 5 biological identities across 12 time intervals. Time intervals assumed circular (e.g., hours day, months year), last interval treated adjacent first. title: Introduction to rosario
text: Use temp_overlap() compute mean pairwise overlaps among rows (biological identities), using chosen index: “pianka” “czekanowski”. returns observed assemblage-wide overlap. assemblage-wide summary informative three biological identities (e.g., individuals, species, communities), captures overall overlap rather pairwise comparisons.
code: temp_overlap(ex1, method = "pianka") #>    pianka  #> 0.9975192  # or  temp_overlap(ex1, method = "czekanowski") #> czekanowski  #>       0.953

title: Introduction to rosario
text: test whether observed overlap differs random expectations, get_null_model() generates null distribution assemblage-wide overlap repeatedly randomizing input matrix using rosario_sample() recomputing mean pairwise overlap (via temp_overlap()). get_null_model() can run simulations parallel setting parallel = TRUE reduce runtime multicore machines. CRAN checks maximum portability, vignette uses parallel = FALSE. recommend using nsim = 1000 applied analyses, runtime depends hardware dataset size.
code: set.seed(1) mod <- get_null_model(ex1, method = "pianka", nsim = 100, parallel = FALSE) mod$p_value #>  #>  One Sample t-test #>  #> data:  res[[1]] #> t = -100.15, df = 99, p-value < 2.2e-16 #> alternative hypothesis: true mean is not equal to 0.9975192 #> 95 percent confidence interval: #>  0.1202562 0.1543425 #> sample estimates: #> mean of x  #> 0.1372993

title: Real-world example
text: rosario package implements null model analysis quantify concurrent temporal niche overlap (.e., activity phenology) among biological identities (e.g., individuals, populations, species) using Rosario randomization algorithm (Castro-Arellano et al. 2010). designed cyclical time data (e.g., hours day, months year) can used assess temporal overlap among two biological identities. vignette provides real-world example showing (1) use external camera-trap dataset, (2) convert detections fixed time bins, (3) build matrix required rosario, (4) run null model test assemblage-wide temporal overlap.

title: Real-world example
text: use subset SIMDeer project (Foster et al. 2020) representing 85,929 capture events three cervid species recorded British Columbia, Canada (51,691 Mule deer, 19,395 Elk, 14,843 White-tailed deer). full dataset available Wildlife Insights (https://app.wildlifeinsights.org/explore). dataset used vignette : Sim_data: CSV file containing capture events (timestamped detections) three cervid species. Note: run vignette locally full data set, download load external data using code . data hosted Figshare. step run automatically comply CRAN policies.
code: options(timeout = 600) download.file("https://ndownloader.figshare.com/files/61985230", destfile = "Sim_data.csv", mode = "wb") Sim_dat <- read.csv("Sim_data.csv") head(Sim_dat)

title: Real-world example
text: rosario workflow requires matrix : rows = biological identities (example: species), columns = time intervals across cycle (example: 30-minute bins across 24-hour day), values = counts (proportions) detections time interval. convert event-level timestamps single row binned counts per species. Time intervals treated circular (e.g., hours day), cycle wraps last interval back first.

what: 3.1. Helper function to bin detections for one species
title: Real-world example
text: function converts timestamps date-time, assigns detection 30-minute bin, returns one-row data frame columns time bins (formatted "HH:MM:SS") values detection counts.
code: bin_species <- function(dat, species_code, bin_mins = 30) {   dat %>%     filter(species == species_code) %>%     mutate(       timestamp = mdy_hm(timestamp),       bin = floor_date(timestamp, "hour") +         minutes(floor(minute(timestamp) / bin_mins) * bin_mins),       hour_min_sec = format(as.POSIXct(bin), "%H:%M:%S")     ) %>%     count(hour_min_sec, name = "count") %>%     tidyr::pivot_wider(       names_from = hour_min_sec,       values_from = count,       values_fill = 0     ) }

what: 3.2. Create binned rows for each cervid species
title: Real-world example
text: generate one binned row per species:
code: mule_deer <- bin_species(Sim_dat, "hemionus") # Mule deer elk <- bin_species(Sim_dat, "canadensis") # Elk wtd <- bin_species(Sim_dat, "virginianus") # White-tailed deer

what: 3.3. Combine species rows into the rosario input matrix
title: Real-world example
text: bind three species rows single matrix. missing time bins filled zeros binning function , ensure entries numeric.
code: binned_df <- dplyr::bind_rows(   MuleDeer = mule_deer,   Elk = elk,   WTD = wtd,   .id = "species" )  # Convert to a numeric matrix (rows = species; columns = time bins) rownames(binned_df) <- binned_df$species data_matrix <- binned_df %>%   select(-species) %>%   mutate(across(everything(), as.numeric)) %>%   as.matrix() rownames(data_matrix) <- binned_df$species  dim(data_matrix)

title: Real-world example

title: Czekanowski overlap index — czekanowski_index
text: Computes Czekanowski index overlap two relative-frequency activity profiles \(p\) \(q\): $$1 - \tfrac{1}{2}\sum_i |p_i - q_i|.$$

title: Czekanowski overlap index — czekanowski_index
text: p Numeric vector non-negative relative frequencies (typically sums 1) describing first biological identity data (e.g. activity, population size, etc) across ordered time bins. Standardized use time intervals manual. q Numeric vector non-negative relative frequencies (length p) second biological identity across ordered time bins.

title: Czekanowski overlap index — czekanowski_index
text: single numeric value [0, 1] 0 indicates overlap 1 indicates identical profiles.

title: Czekanowski overlap index — czekanowski_index
text: Inputs comparable scale; data raw counts, rescale rows proportions first (see rescale_matrix()).

title: Czekanowski overlap index — czekanowski_index
code: set.seed(1) n <- 6 p <- rmultinom(1, 20, rep(1, n))[,1]; p <- p / sum(p) q <- rmultinom(1, 20, rep(1, n))[,1]; q <- q / sum(q) czekanowski_index(p, q) #> [1] 0.65

what: Null-model test via ROSARIO algorithm randomization — get_null_model
title: Null-model test via ROSARIO algorithm randomization — get_null_model
text: Generates null distribution concurrent temporal niche overlap repeatedly randomizing input matrix rosario_sample() recomputing mean pairwise overlap (see temp_overlap()).

title: Null-model test via ROSARIO algorithm randomization — get_null_model
Null-model test via ROSARIO algorithm randomization — get_null_model
text: mat Numeric matrix (rows = biological identities, columns = ordered time intervals). Time intervals assumed circular (e.g., hours day, months year), last interval treated adjacent first. Biological identities can individuals, populations, species communities. method Character string naming overlap index use: "pianka" "czekanowski". nsim Integer number randomizations run (default 100). parallel Logical. TRUE, randomizations executed parallel using furrr::future_map_dfr() multisession plan set internally.

title: Null-model test via ROSARIO algorithm randomization — get_null_model
text: list components: observed_niche_overlap Mean possible pairwise comparisons among biological identities mat. p_value one-sample t.test object comparing null means observed value (mu = observed). null_niche_overlap tibble/data.frame simulated mean overlaps (one per randomization).

title: Null-model test via ROSARIO algorithm randomization — get_null_model
text: "czekanowski", rows rescaled proportions internally satisfy index's assumptions. Randomization preserves row's temporal autocorrelation cyclically shifting (optionally mirroring) profile; see rosario_sample(). parallel = TRUE, function calls future::plan(multisession) internally randomizations distributed across available local sessions. means function overrides previously set future plan. need custom control parallelization (e.g. cluster backends), run non-parallel mode (parallel = FALSE) handle parallelism externally.

title: Null-model test via ROSARIO algorithm randomization — get_null_model
code: get_null_model(ex1, method = "pianka", nsim = 10, parallel = FALSE) #> $observed_niche_overlap #>    pianka  #> 0.9975192  #>  #> $p_value #>  #> 	One Sample t-test #>  #> data:  res[[1]] #> t = -46.004, df = 9, p-value = 5.422e-12 #> alternative hypothesis: true mean is not equal to 0.9975192 #> 95 percent confidence interval: #>  0.1004131 0.1845053 #> sample estimates: #> mean of x  #> 0.1424592  #>  #>  #> $null_niche_overlap #> # A tibble: 10 × 1 #>    pianka #>     <dbl> #>  1 0.109  #>  2 0.147  #>  3 0.0516 #>  4 0.130  #>  5 0.0793 #>  6 0.143  #>  7 0.153  #>  8 0.255  #>  9 0.211  #> 10 0.146  #>

title: Pianka's niche-overlap index — pianka_index
text: Computes Pianka's symmetric index overlap two non-negative activity profiles \(p\) \(q\): $$\frac{\sum_i p_i q_i}{\sqrt{\left(\sum_i p_i^2\right)\left(\sum_i q_i^2\right)}}.$$

title: Pianka's niche-overlap index — pianka_index
text: p Numeric vector non-negative values (counts relative frequencies) first biological identity data 1 (e.g. activity, population size, etc) across ordered time bins. q Numeric vector non-negative values (length p) second biological identity (e.g. activity, population size, etc) across ordered time bins.

title: Pianka's niche-overlap index — pianka_index
text: single numeric value [0, 1]; larger values indicate greater overlap.

title: Pianka's niche-overlap index — pianka_index
text: Pianka's index require inputs sum 1, vectors must non-negative zero.

title: Pianka's niche-overlap index — pianka_index
code: set.seed(1) n <- 10 p <- rpois(n, 3); q <- rpois(n, 3) pianka_index(p, q) #> [1] 0.828351
